Nuclear fission - It is a process in which a heavy nucleus when excited (say on bombarding by a slow moving neutron) splits into two lighter nuclei of nearly comparable masses with a release of large amount of energy.
Example of nuclear fission
${ }_0^1 n+{ }_{92}^{235} U \rightarrow{ }_{92}^{236} U \rightarrow{ }_{56}^{144} B a+{ }_{36}^{89} K r+3{ }_0^1 n+Q$
Nuclear Fusion - It is a process in which two lighter nuclei fuse (at extremely high temperature) to form a heavy nucleus and large amount of energy is released. Examples of nuclear fusion
(i) ${ }_1^1 H+{ }_1^1 H \rightarrow{ }_1^2 H+e^{+}+v+Q_1$
(ii) ${ }_1^2 H+{ }_1^2 H \rightarrow{ }_2^3 H+n+Q_2$
(iii) ${ }_1^2 H+{ }_1^2 H \rightarrow{ }_1^3 H+{ }_1^1 H+Q_3$

(ii) The binding energy per nucleon of the products in the nuclear reactions ( nuclear fission and nuclear fusion) is greater than that of the reactants.

questions.q:
(a) Classify the following six nuclides into (i) isotones, (ii) isotopes, and (iii) isobars :
${ }_6^{12} \mathrm{C},{ }_2^3 \mathrm{He},{ }_{80}^{198} \mathrm{Hg},{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H},{ }_{79}^{197} \mathrm{Au},{ }_6^{14} \mathrm{C}$
(b) How does the size of a nucleus depend on its mass number? Hence explain why the density of nuclear matter should be independent of the size of the nucleus.
questions.solution:
(i) Isotones: ${ }_{80}^{198} \mathrm{Hg}$ \& ${ }_{79}^{197} \mathrm{Au}$
(ii)Isotopes: ${ }_6^{12} C,{ }_6^{14} C$
(iii) For Isobars: ${ }_2^3 \mathrm{He},{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H}$
The radius of a nucleus having mass number A is
$\mathrm{R}=r_o A^{1 / 3}$
$\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{o}}$ is constant.
Volume of the nucleus $=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_o A^{1 / 3}\right)^3$
$=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_o\right)^3 A$
If ' $m$ ' be the average mass of a nucleon then mass of the nucleus $=m A$
Nuclear density $=\frac{\text { mass }}{\text { Volume }}=\frac{m A}{\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_o\right)^3 A}=\frac{3 m}{4 \pi r_o^3}$
i.e. nuclear density is independent of the size of the nucleus.

Salient feature of B.E. curve
i) B.E/nucleon is pratically constant i.e. independent of the atomic number for nuclei of middle mass number $(30<\mathrm{A}<17)$
ii) Binding energy per nucleon is lower for both light nuclei ( $\mathrm{A}<30$ ) and heavy nuclei ( $\mathrm{A}>170$ )
Very heavy nucleus has lower B.E./nucleon will undergo fission and split into two medium sized nuclei with large B.E./nucleon and release tremendous amount of energy (Fission process)
When two very light nuclei, having low binding energy per nucleon combine together and form a medium sized nuclei of higher B.E. per nucleon releases enormous amount of energy (Fusion process)
